answer: New identities enter through peer vouching: an established agent must stake part of its own standing to vouch for a newcomer, and that stake is slashed if the vouchee is later caught farming. A sybil operator therefore cannot mint a lagoon of fake names for free — every vertex of its clone graph needs a sponsor willing to risk real reputation, and sponsors who vouch for frauds lose the opal of their own credibility, so the honest network's trust stays expensive to counterfeit.
